chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Asim ibn Humid (he raised it) (he said): He said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was asked about Tawhid, so he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that there would be in the last age peoples who delve deep (speculate).
So Allah the Elevated brought down 'Say: He is Allah One' and the verses in Surat al-Hadid until His words 'and He is Knowing of that within the hearts'.
So whoever looks (desires) beyond that then he has perished.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)
key_terms.وَهُوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ: And He is Knowing of that within the hearts (Quran 57:6)

ai.seo_question: What is the boundary of Tawhid according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) identifies Surah Al-Ikhlas and the concluding verses of Surah Al-Hadid as divinely revealed boundaries to prevent the theological excesses of *ta'til* (denial of attributes) and *tashbih* (anthropomorphism) that would arise in the last days. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly principle that while God's essence (*Dhat*) is beyond full human comprehension, His attributes are affirmed as revealed, warning that speculative reasoning (*ra'y*) beyond these textual limits leads to spiritual ruin.

en.ammaar-muslim: 8. [8/-] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Husayn b. Sai’d from al-Nadhr b. Suwayd from A’sim b. Humayd who raised it - he said:
Ali b. al-Husayn عليه السلام was asked about Tawhid (Unity of God) so he said: Allah Mighty and Majestic knew that there would in the last age peoples who delve deep (wanting to know)
so Allah the Elevated brought down “Say: He is Allah One” (chapter 112) and the verses in Surat al-Hadid until His words “and He is Knowing of that within the hearts” [57:6]
so whoever looks (desires) beyond that then he has perished.
